title: Read-only maintenance history lookup through an MCP server tool in Copilot Studio
summary: How to give a Copilot Studio agent read-only access to work orders, defects and component history over MCP: tool design, wizard values, allow-list, instructions, a worked repeat-defect example and release limits.
body:
A pattern for letting a Copilot Studio agent read maintenance history (work orders, defect cards, component history) from your CMMS, MRO system or maintenance data platform through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that you or a partner operate. The agent answers questions such as "has this fitting leaked before?" in seconds instead of someone searching three screens. The page behind the link (Microsoft Learn: connect an agent to an existing MCP server) was opened on 20 November 2026. The tool design below is a suggestion for your own server; the Copilot Studio steps follow that page. Nothing here is a release, an approval or a replacement for work cards and approved maintenance data: the agent only retrieves and summarises records for a human planner, engineer or certifying staff member.

=== Prerequisites and version notes ===
- An MCP server that already exists. Copilot Studio supports the Streamable transport; the page says SSE is deprecated and no longer supported after August 2025, so a server that only speaks SSE needs an update.
- Generative orchestration must be on for the agent (new agents have it on by default). The MCP overview page states it as a requirement.
- You need access to the agent's Tools page and, if the server uses OAuth 2.0, the values from your identity provider. API keys are also possible.
- The agent must use the standard harness described on the page. Check in your tenant that the agent you build uses it.
- Access to MCP servers runs through Power Platform connectors, so a data policy that governs connectors also governs this server and its tools. Ask your Power Platform admin before you start.
- Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources, not prompts.

=== Template: server design (example tool names for your own server) ===
Keep the server small and read-only. Four tools are usually enough for a first release:
- search_work_orders: inputs asset_or_registration, free_text (optional), date_from (optional), max_results (default 10). Returns work order number, date, short text, status.
- get_asset_history: inputs asset_id, max_results. Returns chronological history with the repeating findings flagged by your own rule.
- list_open_defects: input asset_id. Returns open defect cards with date raised and deferral reference as stored in your system.
- get_part_stock: input part_number. Returns on-hand quantity per store, nothing else.
Rules for the server: every tool is read-only, returns at most 25 rows, returns identifiers so a human can open the source record, and never returns personal data of mechanics unless your works council agreement allows it (use a role code instead of a name).

Server description to paste into the onboarding wizard (the orchestrator reads this text to decide when to call the server):
Read-only maintenance history for our hangar and plant assets. Use it to find work orders, open defects and the repair history of an aircraft registration, component serial number or machine ID. It cannot create, change or close records and it does not contain approved maintenance data or work cards.

=== Template: wizard values ===
Tools page, Add a tool, New tool, then Model Context Protocol in the Create new section. Fill in:
- Server name: Maintenance History
- Server description: the text above
- Server URL: the HTTPS endpoint of your server (for example https://maintenance-mcp.example.com/mcp)
- Authentication: None only for a test server. For production choose OAuth 2.0 (Dynamic discovery if the server supports Dynamic Client Registration with discovery; otherwise Dynamic or Manual with client ID, client secret, authorization URL, token URL template, refresh URL and optional scopes) so each user reaches the server with their own identity. An API key (Header or Query) is the fallback; the user of the agent then supplies the key.
- If a callback URL appears after Create, copy it into the app registration of your identity provider, then select Next.
- On Add tool select Create a new connection (or an existing one), then Add to agent.

Alternative from the same page: a custom connector in Power Apps built from an OpenAPI file. Example schema, to be adapted:
swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: Maintenance History MCP
  description: Read-only MCP endpoint for work orders, defects and component history (example).
  version: 1.0.0
host: maintenance-mcp.example.com
basePath: /
schemes:
  - https
paths:
  /mcp:
    post:
      summary: Maintenance history, read-only
      x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0
      operationId: InvokeMCP
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Success

=== Template: limit the tools and tell the agent how to use them ===
After the server is added, open it from the agent's Tools tab. By default the Allow all toggle is on. Turn it off, keep the four read tools, select Save and then Publish. With Allow all off, tools that you add to the server later stay off until you enable them, which is what you want for a regulated environment.

Agent instructions (adapt the bracketed parts; type a slash to insert a reference to the tool):
You answer questions from maintenance planners and engineers using the Maintenance History tool.
1. Always call the tool for history questions. Never answer from memory.
2. Ask for the registration, serial number or machine ID if it is missing.
3. Report only what the tool returns, with the work order number for every statement.
4. If the same finding appears at least three times for the same asset, say so and suggest a reliability review. Do not name a cause.
5. You cannot release, close or approve anything. For release statements say: this must be decided by certifying staff using the approved maintenance data.

=== Worked example (invented data) ===
Question: "Has the hydraulic leak at the return-line fitting on ASSET-HYD-07 happened before?" The agent calls search_work_orders and then get_asset_history and finds three records: WO-1041 on 2026-03-02 (seal replaced), WO-1187 on 2026-06-19 (leak at the same fitting) and WO-1302 on 2026-10-08 (leak again). Intervals: 2 March to 19 June is 109 days, 19 June to 8 October is 111 days, mean 110 days. The agent answers: three findings in about seven months, repeating roughly every 110 days, suggested next step a reliability review. It lists the three work order numbers. A planner then opens the records in the source system. All names, numbers and dates are made up for this example.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Leaving Allow all on and exposing a write tool that was added to the server later.
- A vague server description such as "maintenance data". The orchestrator then calls the server for questions it cannot answer.
- Letting the server return free text of defect reports with names of people; this is personal data and may need works council and data protection approval.
- Testing only with your own admin account. Test with a normal planner account; the connection runs with the permissions of the user.
- Trusting a summary of history as an airworthiness statement. It is not one.

=== Adapting it to your environment ===
Replace the tool list with what your CMMS or MRO system can answer cheaply. If you have no server yet, Microsoft's overview page also links to an article on creating one. For plant machinery add get_downtime_events. For aircraft keep the registration as the primary key and return the same fields your records use, so people recognise them. Keep the descriptions of tools short and specific; the page on generative orchestration says the description is the most important selection factor.

=== Security and privacy ===
No secrets in the agent instructions or in the OpenAPI file; client secrets belong in the connection settings. Log tool calls on the server side so you can answer an audit question about who asked for which asset. Check the data policy, the Entra app registration and the data location with your admin. Involve the data protection officer and works council if records contain employee data. For aviation, the Part-145 organisation keeps responsibility for records and release; this agent is a lookup aid only.

title: Index work instructions and maintenance records with Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors
summary: How to choose synced or federated Copilot connectors for plant and MRO content, keep revision and ACL rules intact, and wire the connection into a declarative agent, with a worked file-share example.
body:
How to make controlled shopfloor and maintenance content searchable for Microsoft 365 Copilot and for your agents when it does not live in SharePoint: work instructions on a network share, tickets in a service tool, parts and orders in an ERP, records in a SQL database. Microsoft calls the feature Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (the ingestion mechanism is the Microsoft Graph connectors API). The page behind the link (Microsoft Learn: Copilot connectors overview) was opened on 20 November 2026. The decision table, the source inventory and the revision rule are suggestions for manufacturing and MRO; connector details follow the page.

=== Prerequisites and version notes ===
- Admin rights to deploy connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center, or a developer for a custom connector.
- The page distinguishes synced connectors (content is indexed into Microsoft Graph, tenant configuration by an admin or self-serve configuration where each user authenticates) from federated connectors (data is fetched live through MCP, read-only, user-level OAuth 2.0). Check in your tenant which prebuilt connectors you can use; the page says there are over 100 and names file shares, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, SAP, SQL and Oracle databases among them.
- On-premises sources use the Microsoft Graph connector agent.
- Every indexed item carries an access control list (ACL); Copilot and Search show an item only to people who can open it in the source.
- Copilot Chat is read-only by default. Connectors give it content to read; writing back needs actions or plugins.
- Licensing and the exact feature set change; check the page and your admin center before you promise anything to a plant manager.

=== Template: decision table ===
Source type: synced tenant connector. Use when the content is stable and permissions can be mapped, for example released work instructions and quality manuals on a file share.
Source type: federated connector. Use when the data is volatile or must not be copied, for example live stock or order status, and a federated connector exists for the system.
Source type: self-serve connector. Use when each user should see only what they can reach with their own credentials and a limited amount of recent data is enough.
Source type: custom connector. Use only when nothing prebuilt fits; it needs a schema, an Entra registration and code that you must maintain.

=== Template: source inventory for a plant (fill in per source) ===
Columns: source system; owner; content type; document status values; who may read; revision field; how superseded items are marked; connector type; sync frequency; ACL source (AD group, SharePoint group, none); retention rule; contact for data protection.
Revision rule that matters in regulated production: index only released revisions, or map the revision and status as searchable and retrievable properties, and tell the agent to quote the revision with every answer. A search index that mixes released and superseded work instructions is a quality problem, not a Copilot problem.

=== Template: property mapping for a custom connector (example) ===
- title (searchable, retrievable): document title
- url (retrievable): link to the controlled copy
- docType: work instruction, inspection plan, checklist, drawing note
- revision (retrievable): as printed on the document
- status (searchable, retrievable): released, draft, superseded
- area (searchable): line or cell
- lastReviewed (retrievable): date
Use the properties for refiners and for the agent instructions; check the Graph reference for the exact schema syntax and the label names that your connector needs.

=== Template: use the connection in a declarative agent ===
The declarative agent manifest (schema v1.9) has a GraphConnectors capability. Each connection takes a connection_id and optional narrowing properties. Without a list the agent can use all connectors the user can access, so name the connection explicitly:
{
 "capabilities": [
  {
   "name": "GraphConnectors",
   "connections": [
    {
     "connection_id": "maintdocs"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}
Replace maintdocs with the connection ID that you gave the connection. In Copilot Studio the connector content can be added as a knowledge source for an agent as well.

=== Worked example (invented numbers) ===
A plant has 12,000 PDF work instructions on a file share. A review shows 9,000 are superseded revisions kept for history. Only released revisions are synced: 12,000 - 9,000 = 3,000 items, a reduction of 75 percent. Item ACLs copy the AD groups: Line-3 operators and Planning can read instruction WI-3-017, Purchasing cannot. An operator on Line 3 asks Copilot for the setup steps for WI-3-017 and gets an answer with the document as citation and the revision field in the text; a purchaser asking the same question gets no content from that item. All names and counts are examples.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Syncing everything including drafts and old revisions, then wondering why answers quote retired steps.
- Assuming the index is real time. Synced content follows the sync schedule; check the frequency and the full-crawl option and agree it with the document owners.
- Mapping the ACL to a group that is too broad, which leaks content across lines or customers.
- Using a custom connector for something a prebuilt one covers.
- Forgetting that Copilot citations help people find the source but do not make an answer a controlled document.

=== Adapting it to your environment ===
Start with one source and one user group, such as the work instructions of one line. Measure how many questions get a cited answer, then add the next source. For aviation keep approved maintenance data in its controlled system and index only references or non-controlled aids unless your quality department has approved the use; Copilot output never replaces the manual text or the work card.

=== Security and privacy ===
Connector credentials are service credentials: store them as your admin center requires and rotate them. Never index folders that contain personal files, HR data or customer-restricted drawings without a decision of the data owner. Check export control and customer confidentiality rules for drawings before indexing them. Involve works council and data protection for sources with employee data.

title: Call a CMMS or ERP REST API as an agent tool in Copilot Studio (OpenAPI v2, preview)
summary: Turn a small work order API into Copilot Studio tools: an example OpenAPI v2 file, description wording, wizard steps, a confirmation for the write operation and a worked machine-job example.
